title: Christian Practices: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet how Christians worship: liturgical, non-liturgical and private worship, plus prayer and sacraments.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Christian Practices foundations — worship, prayer, sacraments, the Lord's Prayer.
final_note: You now know the main ways Christians worship and pray.

concepts.def: Set, structured worship with rituals and prayers
Less structured worship, focused on Bible and sermon
Personal prayer, reading and devotion at home
Outward sign of inward grace (e.g. baptism, Eucharist)
Set order of service in formal worship

walkthroughs.body_html:
Liturgical worship (Catholic Mass, CofE) follows a set order with priests, readings and rituals.

Non-liturgical (Baptist, Pentecostal) is less structured — Bible readings, sermon, free prayer and songs.

Private worship happens at home: prayer, Bible reading, devotionals.

The Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9-13) is the prayer Jesus taught his disciples.

'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done.'

It is used in nearly every Christian service, uniting Christians across denominations.

A sacrament is 'an outward sign of an inward grace'.

Catholics and Orthodox recognise seven sacraments: Baptism, Eucharist, Confirmation, Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick, Marriage, Holy Orders.

Most Protestants recognise only two — Baptism and Eucharist — because Jesus directly commanded them in the Gospels.
